text:
Fog and a little mist are hanging on late this morning, with temperatures in the low 40s, but the leftover drizzle is on its way out. The afternoon should be the nicer half of the day. Clouds break up, some sun mixes in, and we top out near 51. That's a decent window for a walk, but don't wait too long, since the sun sets around 4:30.

The next round arrives after dark. Showers move in around 8 tonight and come and go through the night, adding up to about a tenth of an inch, with a low around 42. Monday's wet stretch is the morning, mainly before 9 or 10, then it turns more scattered through the afternoon with another high near 51. The models disagree on how wet Monday gets, and one is much wetter than the rest, so I'd keep the umbrella by the door for the morning commute. Tuesday and Wednesday look mostly drier, with a stray shower and plenty of clouds.

Late in the week, a coastal storm could bring rain mixed with snow Thursday into the weekend, possibly our first real snow. That's still a long way out and could shift.

AFD KEY MESSAGES (forecaster's reasoning, issued 2026-11-08T12:08:00+00:00 — covers the whole BTV area, northern NY included: translate to what Burlington feels, never repeat other regions' place names):
  1. Cooler and unsettled weather will persist through the first half of this week with rounds of showers expected.
  2. Unsettled weather continues through the end of the week, likely trending cooler by next weekend.
AFD WHAT CHANGED (same regional caveat): As of 138 AM EST Sunday... No significant changes were made with this forecast update.
AFD DISCUSSION (the forecaster's full reasoning, same regional caveat; their temps are area-wide ranges):
KEY MESSAGE 1: Precipitation will continue to slowly wind down through the early morning hours as an upper level low pinwheels away to the east. While most of the precipitation is falling as rain or drizzle, temperatures in the higher elevations and portions of the Northeast Kingdom are in the low to mid 30s; our sensor on Mt Mansfield at just short of 4000 ft is reading 28F as of 1 am. Therefore expect these areas are seeing periods of snow, though ground temperatures should be warm enough to preclude any accumulation below 2500 ft. Cameras on some of the higher elevation roads in the Northeast Kingdom courtesy of VTrans do appear to show a bit of snow falling with no accumulation noted, though it's difficult to discern for sure due to darkness and thick fog. These lingering showers will taper to an end by mid to late morning or so, allowing for a dry Sunday afternoon. Highs will be in the low 40s to low 50s, with a bit of a brisk wind at 5 to 15 mph with local gusts to around 20 mph. Additional rounds of showers are expected then through the first half of this week as we remain under the influence of a large upper level low gyrating over eastern Canada. Multiple shortwaves rotating around the base of this low will pivot overhead, keeping the weather unsettled over the next few days. Much like our current system, much of the shower activity will fall as rain, especially during the daylight hours, but some snow will be possible across the higher terrain and portions of the Adirondacks/Northeast Kingdom, especially overnight. Any accumulation will be minimal below 2500 ft, but we'll be watching closely to see if Mt Mansfield is able to break the record for latest 1" of snowfall (Nov 9). Highs will be in the low/mid 40s to low 50s each day, with lows falling into the upper 20s to mid/upper 30s. Winds will remain on the breezy side, but not strong enough to cause any significant impacts. KEY MESSAGE 2: The large Hudson Bay low will continue to dominate the weather across our area, bringing multiple shortwaves into region through the weekend. Wednesday should see lingering, terrain driven mix of rain and snow showers throughout the day. Models on Thursday remain torn on the timing and placement of warm front ahead of the developing low in the Ohio Valley. The solutions could bring a rain- snow mix, or keep things further south and keep our area relatively dry during the day. For Friday and the weekend, models are still keying in on significant closed low swinging down through the Mid- Atlantic region and then up the coastline, bringing several shots of rain and rain/snow mix over the weekend. The current runs are leaning towards a wetter solution for our region which could bring the first significant snow of the season. The details should come into better focus over the next few days.

WCAX METEOROLOGIST (regional station — Burlington relevance only, never their branding): BURLINGTON, Vt. (WCAX) - Any showers have ended for our region, though the outer fringes of the low pressure system are producing snow for Coos County, New Hampshire. The snow may persist until late morning or even midday, with a trace to 3 inches accumulation, though the higher amounts will be in the White Mountains. The rest of today will become partly sunny with highs in the mid-40s to low 50s. The next system will quickly move in Sunday night with more showers. Showers are likely on Monday, especially for the morning. They will become more widely scattered as the afternoon progresses. Highs will be in the 40s with lows in the 30s. Tuesday and Veterans Day looks a little drier now, though a few showers can’t be ruled out both days. Our eyes then turn to a potential coastal storm late in the week, though it can still change as the time is pretty far out. At this time, Thursday is expected to have increasing clouds with a rain/snow mix by afternoon, continuing overnight and through Friday. Some snow accumulation isn’t out of the question, even in the valleys, but there’s still plenty of time for things to change. Showers and mountain snow showers may continue into Saturday with highs mainly in the 30s and lows in the 20s. It’s something we’ll keep an eye on during the week.
NBC5 METEOROLOGIST (2026-11-08T13:52:00Z — same caveat): Seasonably cool Sunday, clouds slowly give way to sun — Sunday looks drier, though patchy drizzle and elevation snowflakes linger early. Expect stubborn clouds through the morning, but more rays of sun should mix in through the afternoon. Highs will be near 50. Clouds increase and scattered showers return this evening into tonight, as a clipper system arrives. Lows reach the 30s and 40s. Monday will be mostly cloudy and cool, as scattered showers continue. Additional mountain flakes are possible, especially for the summits. Highs reach the upper 40s, with a stiff northwest breeze. After a mostly dry start to Tuesday, another round of showers comes through by afternoon. Highs reach the low 50s. Wednesday (Veterans Day) turns drier, with only a spot shower leftover. However, it will be cloudy and cool, with highs in the upper 40s. The late-week stretch looks quite chilly, as the jet stream dips farther south. Highs will be closer to 40, with lots of clouds. A storm system may bring a round of rain and elevation snow Friday into Saturday, but uncertainty remains with the track. Stay tuned for updates.
